title: Quiz Questions
text: Quiz Questions question 1 The cover of Braiding Sweetgrass is designed by ________ and contains an engraving as well as a deckled edge and a bookmark ribbon. The new edition also contains five colorful illustrations by artist ________. question 2 The author, Robin Wall Kimmerer, belongs to the ________ tribe and is trying to learn the language in order to connect with her roots. She and other members of her tribe have felt disconnected from their heritage due to colonialism. This is her way of reconnecting. question 3 Braiding Sweetgrass was published on the 15 th of October 2013 by ________. The hardcover edition of the book has 391 pages. question 4 Kimmerer received her bachelor’s degree in botany from ________ in 1975. She then worked for Bausch & Lomb as a microbiologist, then went on to complete her master’s degree in botany from the University of Wisconsin-Madison in 1979. She also completed her Ph.D. in plant ecology in 1983, after which she began teaching. question 5 Kimmerer is a proponent of ________, which may be described as a cumulative body of knowledge handed down through generations by cultural transmission, about the relationship of living beings with one another and with their environment. She tries to marry TEK with modern science to give a better perspective of the natural world. question 6 Kimmerer’s family was a part of the exodus of Native Americans from their homelands to less fertile lands. Her grandfather, Asa Wall, was forcibly sent to the ________, and deliberately and systematically uprooted from his people and traditional way of life. question 7 True or False: A special hardcover edition of Braiding Sweetgrass was published with a new introduction from Robin Wall Kimmerer in honor of the fortieth anniversary of Simon & Schuster. The book was reissued as an object of meaning that will last for a long time. question 8 True or False: Kimmerer wrote the first draft of the book in purple ink on long yellow legal pads. She likes sitting outside in nature and observing small things in the natural world that can act as microcosms for great ideas while writing the book. question 9 True or False: Kimmerer’s first book is Braiding Sweetgrass: Indigenous Wisdom, Scientific Knowledge and the Teachings of Plants , which was published in 2013 and is the recipient of the 2014 Sigurd F. Olson Nature Writing Award. She wrote the book to gain a better understanding of the plant world. question 10 True or False: Kimmerer considers herself to be raised by mangoes. When she was a child, she would run outside after school with her friends and throw mango seeds at each other. This taught her how to fight. question 11 True or False: The Three Sisters of indigenous agriculture are Brussels sprouts, radishes, and carrots. These three plants together have fed generations of Native Americans throughout North and South America. The three are often planted together and each enhances and supports the other plants. question 12 True or False: Kimmerer tries to recover her lost Potawatomi heritage by communicating more with her community’s elders and holders of knowledge and by learning the Potawatomi language. She also ensures that she attends certain ceremonial events.
